title: Accessibility
steps: Agree WCAG 2.2 Level AA as the target with your team, then audit your current templates and a sample of pages and record each gap.
Build each component and template to meet every Level A and AA success criterion, including visible focus, target size, color contrast, headings, form labels and text alternatives.
Test every template with an automated scan, keyboard-only use and screen readers such as NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver, and log each issue against its WCAG success criterion.
Train your authors to write alternative text, headings, link text and table headers, with a checklist to run before they publish each page.
Set a release gate: each release passes an automated scan and a manual keyboard and screen reader check of changed templates, with no new A or AA failures.
deliverables: Accessibility audit of templates and sample pages
WCAG 2.2 AA test plan and release checklist
Issue log mapped to WCAG success criteria
Author guide and checklist for accessible content
asks: The standard and level you must meet, and any law or policy behind it
An accessibility lead on your side who approves the test plan and signs off each release
risk: New content that falls below AA after launch: we train your authors and give them a checklist to run before they publish each page.
outcome: Your templates are tested against WCAG 2.2 Level AA before launch, and each release is checked the same way, with a record of the results.

facts.text: With AEM, your content authors and site owners can create web content that meets the WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA success criteria.
facts.quote: Using Adobe Experience Manager, content authors and/or website owners can create web content that meets the WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA success criteria
